question: What does 7 // 2 evaluate to in Python according to the course notes?
answer: 7 // 2 evaluates to 3 in Python, as per the notes on integer division [S1].

citations.title: Python Lecture Notes
citations.text: count from the end, so "python"[-1] is "n". Slicing "python"[1:4] returns "yth" (start included, stop excluded).  F-strings embed expressions inside text: f"Total: {price * 2:.2f}" formats a number with two decimals. Integer division // discards the fractional part (7 // 2 is 3), the modulo operator % returns the remainder (7 % 2 is 1), and ** is exponentiation (2 ** 10 is 1024). Dividing with / always returns a float, so 6 / 3 is 2.0.

S5.title: Python Faq Style Addendum
S5.text:
Frequently Asked Questions
Which Python version does the course use? The course uses Python 3.12 in all examples and tests.
Which editor should I use? Any editor is allowed; VS Code is used in the demonstrations.
Is the statistics module allowed in assignments? Yes. statistics.variance(data) returns the sample variance, while statistics.pvariance(data) returns the population variance. In the same way statistics.stdev is the sample standard deviation and statistics.pstdev is the population standard deviation.
Where do I ask questions? Post them on the course forum; answers are usually given within two working days.
